newsitem.title: UK: UK supermarkets on brink of price war, report says.
newsitem.headline: UK supermarkets on brink of price war, report says.

text.p: The risk of a price war between Britain's supermarkets is greater than at any time in the past 15 years, a report released on Monday said.

The report, by independent retail analysts Verdict, said J.Sainsbury Plc needed to regain the initiative from market leader Tesco Plc and might resort to a price war if its current policies failed to restore sales volume growth.
"If Sainsbury's current policies do not succeed in restoring sales volume growth, the temptation to launch a broadside of wide ranging and deep price cuts will be acute," Verdict said.
The report estimated that the probability of a price war breaking out was less than 50 percent, but believed that the price weapon was being "seriously evaluated" as an option.
Verdict said Sainsbury would be the most likely to start a price war, but Tesco could make a pre-emptive strike if it thought Sainsbury was about to open fire.
Sainsbury has been struggling for more than a year to regain the top slot which it lost to Tesco in 1995, but has failed to revive sales convincingly.
Last week it shocked investors with a profit warning, saying pre-tax profits for the current year would be 640 to 650 million stg, well below expectations for profits of more than 700 million.
Verdict predicted Tesco would further extend its market share lead over Sainsbury. "It has over 20 percent more sales area and is steadily narrowing the gap in sales densities."
Tesco has made huge strides in improving product quality, ranging and customer service, which has effectively delivered on promises made by its marketing, Verdict said.
The report said Tesco's Clubcard loyalty scheme had played a big part in boosting sales, but the store's success had more to do with its excellence as a retailer.

Verdict put Tesco's market share in 1996 at 15.3 percent, followed by Sainsbury at 11.8 percent, Safeway Plc and ASDA Group Plc were level third at 7.8 percent, Kwik Save Group Plc fourth with 4.0 percent and Somerfield Plc in fifth place with 3.6 percent. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
